To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
transference is a universal developmental process, and that its systematic therapeutic application is the most powerful tool available to the psychiatrist.

transference occurs in all psychotherapeutic relationships, and is not limited to psychoanalysis; transference is the patient's attempt to repeat a relationship that has been formative in his or her life; the patient's attempt at repetition is a manifestation of his or her unconscious; the therapist's response to the patient's transference attempt is crucial; the therapist's understanding and management of his or her countertransference is the key to the successful management of the patient's transferences.

(1) transference is a ubiquitous phenomenon, (2) transference can be systematically used to facilitate psychotherapy, and (3) transference is the most powerful tool for the psychiatrist in the treatment of psychiatric patients.

a concept of transferences that can be used in all forms of psychotherapy, not just in psychoanalytically oriented psychotherapy.
the study of transference as a universal developmental phenomenon that is systematically utilized in psychotherapy to achieve the therapeutic goals of the treatment process.
the development and testing of a conceptual model of transferences and its psychotherapeutical application in psychiatry.

transference is an essential component of the whole process of psychotherapy, and that its therapeutic use is an indispensable part of the psychotherapist's repertoire.
transference is the universal tendency to repeat formational relationships in the doctor-patients relationship.

transference is a universal phenomenon, that its therapeutic use in psychiatry can be learned, and that its systematic application can greatly enhance the effectiveness of psychiatric care.
